statements.text: [AI] can help in medicine, the development of drugs, efficiency. But it’s affecting our children, it’s affecting education, it’s affecting jobs, it’s affecting the climate. So what we need to do is stop, slow down, make sure we understand all the effects, positive and negative, and that’s why I support Bernie Sanders’ moratorium, so that we can really move forward to make sure that we’re really helping people and not just a profit incentive for the corporations that set them up.
statements.venue: NJ-12 Democratic candidate forum at Princeton (reported by New Jersey Globe)

statements.text: Global cooperation is key to solving so many of the urgent problems facing us -- the climate crisis, public health challenges, the dangerous race towards superintelligent AI -- and it is forums like this one that can help build that cooperative spirit. https://t.co/ybFI1008fl
We need to just kind of make sure that we are doing this correctly, and maximizing the good and minimizing the bad.
statements.venue: New Jersey Monitor interview, on AI generally

statements.text: That’s why we need to pause. If we had a policy, we would implement it. [...] This is a new technology that, just a few years ago, wasn’t on anyone’s radar. And so we need to understand this, and this is why, before we can come up with a policy, we have to understand all these issues and how they impact the things that I talked about.
statements.venue: Interview with The Daily Princetonian, on AI and data center policy
